items.prompt: Choose the relative pronoun. The girl ___ won the race is my cousin.

options.text: which
options.why: Which is used for things and animals, not people.

options.text: where
options.why: Where is used for places.

options.text: who
whose
options.why: Whose shows that something belongs to someone.

hints: The missing word adds information about the girl.
Think about which relative pronoun is used for people.
Ask: is the girl a person, a thing or a place?
items.explanation: Who is used for people. The clause who won the race tells us which girl.

items.prompt: Write who or which. The bicycle ___ I borrowed has a flat tyre.
hints: The missing word adds information about the bicycle.
Who is for people. Think about the word that is used for things.
Ask: is a bicycle a person or a thing?
items.explanation: Which is used for things, so the bicycle which I borrowed is correct. That would also work here.

items.prompt: Which sentence contains a relative clause?

options.text: The dog barks at night.
options.why: This is a simple sentence with one clause.

options.text: The dog that lives next door barks at night.
When the dog barks, I wake up.
options.why: When the dog barks tells us when something happens. It does not add information about a noun.

options.text: The dog barks because it is lonely.
options.why: Because it is lonely gives a reason. It is not a relative clause.

hints: A relative clause adds information about a noun.
Look for who, which, that, whose or where straight after a noun.
Find the word dog in each sentence. What comes straight after it?
items.explanation: That lives next door tells us more about the dog, so it is a relative clause.

items.prompt: Match each beginning to the best ending.
pairs: who helped me with my project.
hints: Each ending starts with a different relative pronoun.
Where goes with places, when with times, who with people and which with things. Whose shows belonging.
Start with the day. Which ending begins with a time word?
items.explanation: Where follows a place (the house), when follows a time (the day), who follows a person (the teacher) and which follows a thing (the book). Whose shows the song belongs to the singer.

items.prompt: Sort the phrases by the relative pronoun that fits the gap.
hints: Look at the noun before each gap.
Ask: is it a person, a thing or a place?
Start with the baker. Is a baker a person, a thing or a place?
items.explanation: People take who (the baker, the pilot), things take which (the umbrella, the song) and places take where (the market, the island).

items.prompt: Join the sentences using whose. I met a boy. His father is a pilot.

answers: I met a boy whose father is a pilot
I met a boy, whose father is a pilot

hints: Whose shows that something belongs to someone.
Whose replaces his, so you do not need his any more.
Find the word in the second sentence that whose will replace.
items.explanation: Whose replaces his and joins the sentences: I met a boy whose father is a pilot.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses commas correctly around the extra information?

options.text: My aunt who lives, in Surabaya is visiting us.
options.why: The commas must go around the whole clause who lives in Surabaya.

options.text: My aunt, who lives in Surabaya is visiting us.
options.why: The extra information needs a comma at the end as well as the start.

options.text: My, aunt who lives in Surabaya, is visiting us.
options.why: The first comma should come after aunt, not after my.

options.text: My aunt, who lives in Surabaya, is visiting us.

hints: Find the extra information first.
Extra information is separated by a comma before it and a comma after it.
Underline who lives in Surabaya in your head. Where should the commas go?
items.explanation: The clause who lives in Surabaya adds extra information about my aunt, so it needs a comma before it and a comma after it.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses a relative pronoun incorrectly?

options.text: The cat which lives next door is very fluffy.
options.why: This is correct. Which can be used for animals.

options.text: The man which fixed our roof was friendly.
The town where I was born is by the sea.
options.why: This is correct. Where is used for places.

options.text: The girl whose bag was lost found it later.
options.why: This is correct. Whose shows the bag belongs to the girl.

hints: Check each relative pronoun against the noun in front of it.
Remember: who for people, which for things and animals, where for places, whose for belonging.
Start with the man. Which pronoun should be used for a person?
items.explanation: A man is a person, so the sentence should say the man who fixed our roof. Which is for things and animals.

items.prompt: Write the missing relative pronoun. Komodo Island, ___ is in Indonesia, is home to the largest lizard in the world.
hints: The missing word adds extra information about a place.
The clause is between commas, so that cannot be used here.
Ask: is Komodo Island a person or a thing? Then choose the pronoun.
items.explanation: The extra information is about an island, so which is used. That cannot start a clause between commas.

items.prompt: Read: The pupils who finished early read quietly. What does this sentence tell us?

options.text: Only some pupils finished early, and those pupils read quietly.
All the pupils finished early.
options.why: Without commas, the clause picks out some pupils, not all of them.

options.text: The pupils read quietly because the teacher asked them to.
options.why: The sentence does not give a reason.

options.text: The pupils finished reading early.
options.why: Finished early is about their work, and reading came afterwards.

hints: Notice that there are no commas around who finished early.
A clause without commas tells us which ones we are talking about.
Ask: does the sentence mean every pupil, or only certain pupils?
items.explanation: Without commas, who finished early tells us which pupils read quietly: only the ones who finished early. With commas, it would mean all the pupils finished early.

items.prompt: Which word begins the relative clause? The boy who sat beside me was new.

options.text: who
boy
options.why: Boy is the noun the clause describes.

options.text: sat
options.why: Sat is the verb inside the clause.

options.text: beside
options.why: Beside is a preposition.

hints: A relative clause gives extra information about a noun.
It begins with a word such as who or which.
Find the word that links the clause to the noun boy.
items.explanation: Who sat beside me is the relative clause. It describes the boy.

items.prompt: Write which or that. The mango ___ fell from the tree was ripe.
hints: The clause describes a thing, not a person.
Who is for people.
Choose a word for things.
items.explanation: Which and that both work for things. Who is for people.

items.prompt: The park ___ we played football is near the school.
hints: The park is a place.
We played football in the park.
Where can replace in the place where.
items.explanation: Where refers to a place.

items.prompt: Build the sentence.
items.answer: The boy who lives next door plays football.
hints: Start with The boy.
The relative clause comes straight after boy.
Football is the last word.
items.explanation: Who lives next door tells us which boy.

items.prompt: Match each relative pronoun to what it refers to.
hints: Think of a noun for each.
Whose shows ownership.
Where is about places.
items.explanation: Who is for people, which for things, whose shows ownership and where is for places.

items.prompt: Put the parts in order to make a sentence.
hints: The clause comes straight after the noun it describes.
Which Sekar painted tells us about the picture.
The main verb hangs follows the clause.
items.explanation: The relative clause which Sekar painted goes right after the picture.

items.prompt: Write when or where. Saturday is the day ___ we visit our grandparents.
hints: Saturday is a day, a time.
Where is for places.
The clause tells us about the day.
items.explanation: When is used after nouns about time.

items.prompt: Sort the sentences by how they use commas.

items.text: Bali, which is an island, is popular.
My aunt, who lives in Medan, called me.
The Nile, which is long, flows north.
The girl who won the race is my cousin.
The shoes that I bought are too small.
Pupils who finish early may read.

hints: Extra information could be removed without changing the main idea.
Needed information tells us which one.
Look for commas on both sides.
items.explanation: Extra information goes inside commas. Needed information has no commas.

items.prompt: Citra visited the village ___ her grandmother was born. A guide, ___ name was Joko, showed her a boat ___ was over a hundred years old.
hints: Place, ownership, thing.
Check each noun before the gap.
Name belongs to the guide, so use whose.
items.explanation: Where is for places, whose shows ownership, and which is for things.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses whose correctly?

options.text: I know a girl whose she has a red bike.
options.why: Whose already includes the idea of belonging. Do not add she.

options.text: I know a girl whose bike is red.
I know who’s bike is red.
options.why: Who’s means who is. Use whose for ownership.

options.text: I know a girl whose.
options.why: The clause is not finished.

hints: Whose shows ownership.
It replaces his, her or their.
Check which sentence has no extra pronoun.
items.explanation: Whose connects the girl with the bike she owns.

items.prompt: Write the missing relative pronoun. The bridge, ___ crosses the river, is very old.
hints: The clause is extra information inside commas.
The bridge is a thing.
That is not used in a clause set off by commas.
items.explanation: Which is used for things when the clause is inside commas.

items.prompt: Tom has only one brother. Which sentence is correct?

options.text: Tom’s brother who plays chess lives in Bali.
options.why: Without commas, this suggests Tom has several brothers.

options.text: Tom’s brother, who plays chess, lives in Bali.
Tom’s brother, that plays chess, lives in Bali.
options.why: That is not used with commas for people.

options.text: Tom’s brother who, plays chess lives in Bali.
options.why: The comma is in the wrong place.

hints: One brother means the clause only adds extra detail.
Extra detail goes inside commas.
Choose the sentence with commas on both sides.
items.explanation: Commas show that who plays chess is extra information about the only brother.

items.prompt: In which sentences could that replace which?

options.text: The cake which Mum baked was delicious.
Java, which is an island, has many volcanoes.
options.why: That cannot be used after a comma in this way.

options.text: The books which we ordered arrived today.
Mount Bromo, which is in East Java, is famous.
options.why: That cannot be used after a comma in this way.

options.text: The song which Wulan sang won first prize.

hints: That can replace which when the clause is needed information.
Clauses inside commas cannot use that.
Check for commas.
items.explanation: That works in the sentences without commas.

items.prompt: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?

options.text: Mr Hadi whose dog barks all night is moving.
options.why: Extra information about a named person needs commas.

options.text: Mr Hadi, whose dog barks, all night is moving.
options.why: The commas are in the wrong place.

options.text: Mr Hadi whose, dog barks all night, is moving.
options.why: The commas are in the wrong place.

options.text: Mr Hadi, whose dog barks all night, is moving.

hints: The clause is extra information about a named person.
It needs commas around it.
Check where the clause starts and ends.
items.explanation: The clause whose dog barks all night is extra information, so it goes inside commas.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?

options.text: This is the room which I sleep.
options.why: Which needs in before it, or use where.

options.text: This is the room who I sleep.
options.why: Who is for people.

options.text: This is the room in which I sleep.
This is the room whose I sleep.
options.why: Whose shows ownership and does not fit here.

hints: Think about what the clause says about the room.
Which needs a preposition when the room is the place.
The room is a place, so look for in which or where.
items.explanation: In which means the same as where.

items.prompt: True or false: In the sentence "The boy who won the race is my cousin", the words "who won the race" are a relative clause.

options.text: True
False

hints: Which noun does it tell us about?
It starts with who.
It describes the boy.
items.explanation: A relative clause gives extra information about a noun. Who won the race tells us about the boy.

items.prompt: True or false: The relative pronoun which is used for people only.

options.text: True
False

hints: Which word is for people?
Think of the book which I read.
Which is for things.
items.explanation: Which is used for things or animals. Who is used for people.

items.prompt: True or false: In the sentence "The girl whose bag was lost cried", the word whose shows belonging.

options.text: True
False

hints: What belongs to the girl?
Whose is about owning.
Whose shows belonging.
items.explanation: Whose shows that something belongs to someone. The bag belonged to the girl.

items.prompt: True or false: In the sentence "The house where I grew up is old", the word where refers to a person.

options.text: True
False

hints: Does where mean a place?
Which noun comes before where?
It refers to the house.
items.explanation: Where refers to a place. The house is the place.

items.prompt: True or false: A relative clause gives extra information about a noun.

options.text: True
False

hints: What does it describe?
It joins to a noun.
Extra information.
items.explanation: A relative clause adds detail, for example The dog that barked was brown tells us about the dog.

items.prompt: True or false: The sentence "The book that I read it was good" is correct.

options.text: True
False

hints: Does the clause need it?
That already refers to the book.
Remove the extra word.
items.explanation: The word it is not needed because that already stands for the book. The correct sentence is The book that I read was good.

items.prompt: The girl ___ won the race is my cousin.

options.text: which
whose
who

hints: The clause is about a person.
Which is for things.
Who is for people.
items.explanation: We use who for a person.
